nodes.label: Electrochemical methods

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What scan rates were employed for the electrochemical tests in the study?
nodes.answer: The scan rates used were 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, and 250 mVs⁻¹.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What electrochemical experiments were conducted and which device was used?
nodes.answer: Electrochemical experiments were conducted using a manually connected Nova 2.1.5 model Autolab (PGSTAT128N) device.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which electrolyte solutions were used for the electrochemical analyses?
nodes.answer: The electrolyte solutions used were 1 M H2SO4, 1 M NaOH, and 1 M Na2SO4.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_003
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: In the context of MFCs, what are some of the abbreviations related to electrochemical processes listed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Some of the abbreviations related to electrochemical processes include EAB (Electrochemically active bacteria), MECs (Microbial electrolysis cells), and MFCs (Microbial fuel cells).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Why do metallic and carbonaceous materials lack efficiency in MFCs?
nodes.answer: They lack sufficient electrochemical active sites to facilitate extracellular electron transfer (EET) between the anode and exoelectrogens, and their flat surfaces reduce the contact area with electrochemically active microbes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What are the implications of nanomaterials on electrode characteristics in microbial fuel cells (MFCs)?
nodes.answer: The types of nanomaterials can affect the electrode's homogeneity, surface hydrophobicity, and surface charge, which influence the interaction between the anode and bacteria, ultimately affecting the MFC's capacity to produce electricity.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What method was employed for the functionalization of the electrode materials?
nodes.answer: A hydrothermal method was used for the functionalization of the electrode materials.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What methods were employed to analyze the structural properties of the prepared electrodes?
nodes.answer: The structural properties were analyzed by XRD and FTIR.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which technique was used to analyze the surface morphology of the electrodes?
nodes.answer: The surface morphology of the electrodes was analyzed using FESEM.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_009
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which electrolyte solution was used for the electrochemical measurements in the study?
nodes.answer: A 1 M Sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) electrolyte solution was used for the electrochemical measurements.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_010
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What methods were used to test the electrochemical performance of the electrodes?
nodes.answer: The methods used were cyclic voltammetry (CV), galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) tests, and electrochemical impedance spectrometry (EIS).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_011
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What method was used to perform electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements?
nodes.answer: EIS measurements were performed at open circuit potential with an AC amplitude of 5 V at frequencies ranging from 0.1 Hz to 100 kHz.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Water purification techniques|Electrochemical methods_qna_012
nodes.label: Science and Tech
nodes.question: What method did Lavas et al. propose for treating industrial textile wastewater, and what were the results?
nodes.answer: Lavas et al. proposed the CC-EO (Sequential Chemical Coagulation-Electro-Oxidation) method for treating industrial textile wastewater, which eliminated 100% of colour, 75% of TOC, and 93.5% of COD in a 43-minute electrolysis process at a cost of 6.91 USD.
